support_spans: How do I use PndMasterRecoTask in the generic workflow?
runtime_points.text: How to use PndMasterRecoTask in the generic workflow

claims.claim_text: In the PandaRoot generic workflow, PndMasterRecoTask serves as a master wrapper task that bundles and configures the default reconstruction tasks—including barrel tracking, forward tracking, and Kalman fitting—for use in reconstruction macros.

PndMasterRecoTask is instantiated by invoking its constructor with an option string (such as PndMasterRecoTask(TString fOptions = "")), where passing an empty string selects the default full setup, or specific flags (such as "day1", "multikalman", "genfit2", "newGF2", or "ftstrack") can be combined to configure detector configurations and tracking/fitting algorithms.

During construction, PndMasterRecoTask evaluates the options string, creates and configures the appropriate subtasks (such as PndBarrelTrackFinder, PndTrkTracking2, forward straw tracking, and Kalman filter tasks), and registers them internally via Add((TTask *)task) so they run in the reconstruction pipeline.

support_spans: What is the theoretical purpose of the DPM elastic-scattering model?
runtime_points.text: The theoretical purpose of the DPM elastic-scattering model

claims.claim_text: The Dual Parton Model (DPM) serves as a phenomenological framework to describe high-energy antiproton-proton elastic scattering, specifically modeling the hadronic amplitude that cannot be calculated from first principles across a wide range of four-momentum transfers (|t|).

Unlike simple exponential parameterizations that are only valid at small |t| and fail to describe complex diffractive structures such as dips and secondary maxima at larger |t|, the DPM formulation captures diffractive features and yields non-zero differential cross sections at higher momentum transfers without relying on unstable free parameters.

In the PANDA Luminosity Detector (LMD) framework, the hadronic amplitude from the DPM model is combined with the Coulomb amplitude to form the full elastic differential cross section, enabling stable and reliable luminosity extraction even in higher beam-momentum and higher |t| regimes where the hadronic contribution dominates.
